The paper was published on September 14, 2017 in Mathematical Models and Methods in Applied Sciences, Volume 27, Number 12, pages 2229-2259.
The authors are Carlos Jerez-Hanckes (Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile), Christoph Schwab, and Jakob Zech (both from ETH Zurich).
The paper proves shape holomorphy for time-harmonic electromagnetic wave scattering from perfectly conducting and dielectric obstacles.
Shape holomorphy enables dimension-independent convergence rates for sparse approximation techniques in uncertainty quantification.
The analysis uses weighted Hilbert spaces H_κ(curl, D^c) that incorporate Silver-Müller radiation conditions.
Domain transformations are required to be bijective, bi-Lipschitz maps in W^{1,∞}(D̂, ℝ³).
The curl operator transforms under domain mappings according to Û = dT^⊤(U∘T), where dT is the Jacobian of T.
The paper uses bilinear (not sesquilinear) inner products to ensure holomorphy of the parametric solution maps.
Existence and uniqueness of solutions is established using Helmholtz decomposition, Fredholm alternative, and unique continuation results.
The approach extends beyond first-order perturbation analysis to handle large shape variations without topology changes.
Tangential trace operators γ_D and γ_N map from H(curl, D) and H(curlcurl, D) to H^{-1/2}(∂D).
The paper considers both perfectly conducting (PC) and dielectric (DE) scattering problems.
Maxwell equations are formulated with material parameters ε (permittivity), μ (permeability), and σ (conductivity).
The wave number is defined as κ² = ω²με + iωμσ, where ω is the circular frequency.
Shape Taylor expansions of far-field patterns converge in a vicinity of the nominal domain for fixed amplitude perturbations.
The results justify the use of high-order quasi-Monte Carlo methods for computing ensemble averages over uncertain shapes.
Sparse adaptive collocation approximation algorithms can compute dimensionally adaptive polynomial chaos surrogates of scattered EM fields.
The paper establishes that scattered fields are strongly measurable in weighted spaces for random geometric perturbations.
Green's formula for H(curl, D) relates volume integrals to boundary integrals through tangential trace operators.
The analysis applies to countably-parametric regular scattering surfaces with holomorphic parameter dependence.
The work extends linearized domain perturbation approaches used in first-order second moment (FOSM) uncertainty quantification.
Unique continuation results play a crucial role in establishing injectivity of Maxwell operators.
The paper uses Lemma 2.1 to decompose the Maxwell operator into components whose isomorphism properties can be verified separately.
Domain transformations must preserve Lipschitz regularity of boundaries to maintain well-posedness of scattering problems.
The approach enables model order reduction and reduced basis approximations for parametric EM scattering problems.
